question: Your team drafts hundreds of short, routine customer replies daily, and cost and speed matter more than nuance. Occasionally a complex escalation needs careful reasoning. What is the sound model strategy?
A developer wants Claude Code to auto-approve a few commands on their own machine without changing the permissions their teammates get from the repository.
A finance owner wants a hard monthly stop on the spend of one team. The team's API keys currently sit in the Default Workspace. Which change meets the constraint?
A support chatbot answers each message on its own, so follow-up answers ignore earlier turns. The model must stay the same. Which change meets the constraint?
A new agent loops overnight and drives API spend up. The team shares one organization across three projects. The team needs a monthly ceiling for each project and a stop for a single runaway loop.
A compliance dashboard must count declined requests by policy area. The team cannot change the model. Which method meets the constraint?
A project team needs a monthly spend cap for its own traffic only. The cap must not include traffic from other teams. Which setup meets the constraint?
A company runs one workspace for each team. The owner wants a monthly budget for each team and rate limits for each model. Select two settings that meet both requests.
A team runs development and production traffic in one shared workspace. The team needs separate rate limits and separate cost reports for each environment. Select two changes that meet both requests.
